### 2. Incident Overview
* **Scenario Type:** Sub-Agent Blocker (defense-in-depth follow-up to b8c8-8566-646e-4b61)

#### Expected Behavior
When the harness reaps an isolation:worktree before harvest, the orchestrator should attempt to RECOVER the agent's work (e.g., fetch the pushed worktree branch, re-dispatch, or pull staged files from the session worktree) before giving up.

#### Actual Behavior
per-worktree-review-commit.md Step 1a (and single-agent-integrate.md Step 1) only HALT (exit 1 + ticket comment + git branch -D) on a reaped worktree — no recovery path. Confirmed during b8c8-8566 ADVANCED investigation; historical lens noted predecessor 907d-7242-516d-49cc landed only this HALT defense while its prescribed Option A (retention staging on all isolated agents) went unimplemented until b8c8. The retention-staging fix (b8c8) prevents the trigger; this ticket tracks the recover-on-reap backstop so a reap that still fires does not lose work. Depends on agent worktree branches being pushed (not currently done).
data.title: per-worktree-review-commit.md: 907d reaped-worktree check -> HALT-only, no recovery of harvestable work
